page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, a dedicated CPU allocation, and a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n2-highmem-4 delivers modest computational performance. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also rank in the bottom 25%, though the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating in the middle 50%. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level, while more complex tasks such as image processing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show poor performance, landing in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highmem-4 is its high memory allocation relative to its lower-tier processing capabilities. While it provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput, it is less suitable for compute-heavy operations, as evidenced by its weak database operations and static web serving benchmarks. This instance is best suited for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity with low CPU demands, such as small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight memory-intensive applications.
